approach.method_basis: The reference is the current Anchor: a task-local genetic search over molecular graphs with a learned ranker placed in front of the oracle. Each announced batch of ten refits a Gaussian process on every molecule this session has had scored, using integer-count Morgan environment features and a generalized Tanimoto kernel. The breeder then builds a complete fresh field of 160 de novo offspring for that one batch: breeding parents are drawn from high-scoring population quantiles, about forty-five percent of attempts recombine a connected fragment of two parents with an optional finishing edit, and the rest apply a short run of successive atom, bond and ring edits to a single parent, the run length being drawn as one, two or three calls with probabilities 0.82, 0.15 and 0.03 and stopping early if an edit fails. Every product must pass a stable canonical identity check, two duplicate scopes and a narrow rule forbidding sulfur environments its own generating parents did not carry. A single correlated draw from the joint posterior over that field then picks the ten molecules to evaluate, masking each winner before the next position. Accepted scores return to the archive and to a greedily maintained population of the sixty-four best molecules. On top of that loop the most recent Child added a stall rule: once three consecutive announced batches fail to improve the session's best molecule, only the forty highest posterior-mean members of the field remain eligible, and the full field returns on the first improving batch. The breeder also carries a second, much older effort rule that nothing has ever measured: while one candidate slot keeps failing, the single-parent route raises the minimum number of successive edits it must make - one more edit for every eighty consecutive failed attempts on that slot, capped at six - and takes the larger of that floor and the sampled run length. A slot's counter resets as soon as it admits a candidate.
approach.novelty: Nothing is added. One law is removed, and the interesting part is the prediction that removing it changes nothing at all: the rejection-conditioned minimum edit count disappears, so the single-parent route's run length is exactly the sampled one, two or three calls, while the sampled law itself, the early stop on a failed edit, the slot counter and its reset, the separate crossover attenuation that uses the same counter, the sulfur gate, identity admission, the archive, the ranker and the stall rule all stay exactly as inherited. This is the only contribution debt on this Anchor that can be paid without also paying for a different search path: the Parent's own receipts show the slot counter never passes five while the first escalation threshold is eighty, so the removed term was returning its neutral value at every one of its tens of thousands of opportunities, and the random stream is consumed in the same order with it gone. The pre-registered outcome is therefore bit-exact reproduction of all fifteen sessions and a paired delta of exactly zero, read as a no-material-effect conditional contribution with its exposure receipt - and the experiment is a genuine test, because any divergence falsifies the recorded dormancy claim and the receipts say at which slot count the floor actually bound. That separates it from every sibling on this lineage: the one sibling on this Anchor changed when the stall regime releases and lost 0.0079, and the earlier removals all deleted laws that fire constantly - the sampled continuation itself (-0.030700), crossover (-0.043640), count multiplicity (-0.038795), residual correlation (-0.050545) - and each paid a departure cost that swamped what it was trying to measure.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent is the new formal Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d: complete matched panel macro mean 0.607030316211131, population SD 0.030175277546149237, seed macros 0.649701282562401 / 0.585233817344553 / 0.586155848726439, per-task means zaleplon_mpo 0.4375952611706346, deco_hop 0.7073702253375034, drd2_docking 0.984572059462962, median_2 0.22882968965773362, sitagliptin_mpo 0.6767843454268235, paired +0.010577201922441012 over its own code Parent n-1744a1494180 and positive on all three seeds (+0.006603, +0.022061, +0.003067). What limits this Parent is not an allocator behaviour but the state of its own account: it retains seven mechanisms and the frozen catalog records ten contribution gaps on it, nine of them carrying only condition-mismatched evidence from the mask-free Parent, and four of those nine already sit inside the ungated law-free departure band measured by n-1c2f17550a3e (reference -0.009888, band [-0.050871, +0.031095]): optional continuation -0.030700, count multiplicity -0.038795, residual correlation -0.050545 and connected-fragment crossover -0.043640 (h-89a135599fc573a6, h-a81d80c6e32c84d8), so repeating them on this Anchor would buy departure rather than attribution. One gap is different: m-000000000015, rejection-conditioned mutation-call escalation, has needs_evidence true and an empty evidence list - no node anywhere has ever removed or exercised it - and the behaviour it names is measurably idle on this Parent. Reading the Parent's own fifteen stderr sessions read-only and reconstructing the per-member attempt counter the floor reads (count each in-loop breed receipt once, excluding the re-logged emitted receipts; member_attempts equals the attempt index minus the attempt index of the last pooled admission in the same announced batch) gives 76,057 in-loop breeding attempts, of which 69,600 were pooled, 6,316 duplicate, 138 sulfur-rejected and 3 invalid. The counter takes the value 1 in 69,600 attempts, 2 in 5,781, 3 in 607, 4 in 61 and 5 in 8; its maximum over all fifteen sessions is 5 and the longest preceding rejection run is 4, against a first escalation threshold of 80. In the 41,688 attempts that actually took the ordinary single-parent mutation route the floor min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80) therefore evaluated to exactly 1 at every single position, so max(sampled_length, floor) returned the separately sampled [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] length unchanged every time and the escalation branch has never added one mutate call. Curate records the same absence from its side (h-c89025d9833677c2: saturation floor one only, escalation above floor one was never exposed) and the catalog records the thresholds as unreached, but both are code inspection, not experiment. The Anchor thus carries, in a source of 1,198 complexity units, a law that has never fired, that no experiment has ever priced, and that every future removal on this composition must keep in its retained-mechanism list without being able to account for it.
hypothesis: Remove the rejection-conditioned minimum on the number of successive graph-mutation calls taken by the ordinary single-parent mutation route of the Anchor's breeder. In the Parent that route performs max(sampled_length, min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80)) successive mutate calls, where sampled_length is drawn once per attempt from [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] over one, two and three calls and member_attempts counts the consecutive construction attempts since this announced batch last admitted a pool member; after the removal it performs exactly sampled_length calls. Nothing else is touched: the sampled law, the break at the first failed mutate call, the discard of an attempt that produced no edit, the member_attempts counter itself with its increment per attempt and its reset to zero on pool admission, the separate halving of crossover probability while member_attempts exceeds forty, crossover and its finishing edit, the sulfur gate, identity admission, both duplicate scopes, the attempt bound and its partial-pool break, the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process, the correlated draw with its sequential availability masks, the stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility mask with K=3 and M=40, the archive and the greedy survivor population all remain exactly as inherited. The causal claim has two steps. First, the removed term is the only consumer of the escalation threshold and draws no randomness, so if member_attempts never reaches eighty the deleted expression returned its neutral value 1 at every evaluation, the realized call length is identical at every position, every random stream is consumed at the same positions, and all fifteen sessions must reproduce the Anchor record for record. Second, this is the measurement the catalog gap needs: an exactly reproducing panel with an exposure receipt showing the threshold was never approached classifies this mechanism's conditional total endpoint contribution as no-material-effect on this composition, while any record-level divergence falsifies the recorded unreached-threshold claim and the same receipt names the slot count at which the floor bound.

finding_summary.headline: Removing the rejection-conditioned mutation-call floor changed nothing: its trigger was never approached and all fifteen sessions reproduce the Anchor exactly
finding_summary.insights:
The campaign now has an experimental answer where it had an empty evidence list: rejection-conditioned mutation-call escalation contributes nothing on this Anchor, and it contributes nothing for a specific and checkable reason - its trigger is sixteen times further away than this benchmark's rejection statistics ever get. The admission path is simply too permissive for it: 69,600 of 76,057 attempts are admitted on the first try, so a candidate slot almost never fails twice in a row, let alone eighty times. This is a dormancy result, which is stronger than a measured null under exposure: the removed expression returned its neutral value at every one of its 41,688 opportunities, so no random draw moved and the reproduction is exact rather than merely similar. It also closes the one contribution gap on this Anchor that could be paid without buying path departure - the four other candidate removals all sit inside the law-free departure band, where a removal's loss cannot be separated from the cost of leaving the Parent's trajectory.

Two corollaries come free. First, complexity accounting: every later arm on this composition has been carrying this law in its retained-mechanism list and can now drop it, and the same audit shows the second law keyed to the same counter - the halving of crossover probability above forty consecutive failures - was likewise never reached, since the counter never passed five. That is an exposure finding, not a contribution measurement of that law, but it says a removal of it would also be a dormancy test rather than a search-behaviour change. Second, the only way this identity could ever be priced on this method is to change the admission statistics it reads - a much harsher gate, a far larger pool target or a stricter identity rule - which is a different experiment, and nothing here transfers to the L07 variant with its threshold of eight, to a lower threshold or to a different cap. A reproduction this exact is also a second, independent confirmation that this harness is deterministic under a fixed seed and profile, which is what makes future removals on this Anchor readable at all.

Because the molecules are the Parent's molecules exactly, the molecular reading is a second look at the same output and it is where the real limitation sits. Each session collapses onto one substituted scaffold - 12 to 21 distinct Murcko scaffolds in the top-scoring decile against 187 to 560 over the full proposal set, with 83 of one objective's best 87 molecules coming from a single seed - and then keeps editing it. This node's own receipts show why: of the 5,830 generating-parent entries behind those 4,350 proposals, 4,349 come from the population's top quantile, 1,211 from the second and 270 from the third; 1,595 of the 4,350 proposals were bred entirely from molecules first seen in the immediately preceding announced batch, the mean age of the oldest generating parent is 2.9 batches, only 2.6 percent reach back ten or more batches and just 198 descend from an initial-population member, so the search is a short-memory walk around the current leader. The late budget is spent on relabelling: 253 of 4,350 evaluations improved their session's best, 62 percent of the total gain lands in the first third against 12 percent in the last, and one session (zaleplon_mpo, seed 1) made its last improvement at evaluation 87 and then spent 203 further evaluations with 32 of its last 98 proposals sitting in five-way-or-larger exact score ties - families that differ only in whether a position carries F, Cl or Br. The surrogate is not the thing that is broken: within each announced batch the posterior mean's ranking of the ten molecules it selected agrees with their realized scores at a mean Spearman of 0.515 (median 0.553, negative in only 30 of 435 batches), consistent with the Anchor's own recorded pair-ordering accuracy of 0.799. What the evidence supports is a proposal-and-population limitation, not a ranking-model limitation: the method has no way to hold several structurally distinct families alive at once and no skeleton-level edit available at comparable frequency to peripheral substitution. The kind of method that would remove it is a population with explicit structural niching or scaffold-distance-aware admission, together with proposal operators that act on the skeleton (ring replacement, linker length, fusion pattern, scaffold hop) and with constructive introduction of whole functional-group classes - not a retuned threshold anywhere in the existing laws. The nine other recorded contribution gaps on this Anchor stay open and condition-mismatched, and this node says nothing about any of them.
finding_summary.results:
The exposure audit is the primary reading and it is unambiguous. Reconstructing the per-member rejection counter from this node's own breed receipts over all fifteen sessions gives 76,057 in-loop construction attempts (69,600 pooled, 6,316 duplicate, 138 sulfur-rejected, 3 invalid). The counter takes the value 1 in 69,600 attempts, 2 in 5,781, 3 in 607, 4 in 61 and 5 in 8; its maximum anywhere is 5 and the longest preceding rejection run is 4, against a first escalation threshold of 80. Per session the maximum is 3 to 5, never higher. Not one of the 76,057 attempts reached 80, and in the 41,688 attempts that actually took the ordinary single-parent mutation route there are zero positions at which the inherited floor would have exceeded that position's sampled call length. Recomputing the same audit read-only over the Parent's fifteen sessions returns every one of those figures identically, so the catalog's recorded unreached-threshold condition is now measured rather than inferred from code.

With the floor gone the ordinary route's realized call count is exactly the separately sampled length: 34,210 one-call, 6,245 two-call and 1,233 three-call runs over 41,688 positions, empirical shares 0.8206 / 0.1498 / 0.0296 against the declared 0.82 / 0.15 / 0.03 law, with zero runs stopped early by a failed edit and 78,396 operator calls in total - all identical to the Parent position by position.

The divergence check finds no divergence anywhere. All fifteen trajectory files are byte-identical to the Parent's published trajectories: the same 150 initial records, the same 4,350 optimizer proposals in the same order with the same scores, the same best-so-far path and the same final Top-1. All fifteen session logs are identical line for line - 164,935 lines per side, about 740 MB - once the four wall-clock timing fields are removed, which means every pool, every posterior fit, every selected index, every sampled value and every gate decision matched: 435 pools at 160 of 160 with no truncation and 76,057 breeding attempts, 435 batches each emitting ten unique identities with no posterior fallback, 4,350 selection receipts, and the stall regime restricting the same 88 of 435 announced batches in the same 13 of 15 sessions with deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 again never restricted. The configuration block logged at session start is identical key for key.

The endpoint panel is therefore equal cell for cell: all fifteen cells complete with 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals, seed macros 0.649701 / 0.585234 / 0.586156 and macro mean 0.607030, paired delta exactly 0.000000 on every seed and every task, which at the 0.002 descriptive scale is read as no material effect and never as statistical equivalence. On the implementation side the diff against the Anchor is exactly the two deleted lines, restoring the one statement reproduces the Anchor's source hash byte for byte, no occurrence of the escalation term survives, and no configuration key, receipt field, asset or dependency changed.

molecular.headline: All fifteen sessions reproduce the Parent record for record: halogen-decorated fused heteroaromatics whose leaders carry N-halogen and aminal groups
molecular.overall_character: This node's chemistry is the Parent's chemistry exactly. All 15 staging trajectory files under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-2/runs/staging are byte-identical to the published Parent trajectories for n-61b9b3bfb40d (cmp over seed 0/1/2 x five tasks), the context comparison reports paired_mean_delta 0.0 and a per-task delta of 0.0 on every seed, and my own structural reading of the 4,350 optimizer proposals reproduces the Parent assessment's counts to the molecule (888 N-halogen, 162 O-halogen). So nothing below is new chemistry; it is a second, independent reading of the same molecules. What they are: mid-sized, heavily ring-fused, strongly aromatic molecules - mean 24.3 to 31.6 heavy atoms and MW 365 to 461 by task, 3.0 to 4.8 rings of which 2.1 to 3.7 are aromatic, digest ring_closure_rate 0.971 to 0.986 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.964 to 0.977. They are built almost entirely from carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and halogen: digest charged_rate is 0.0 and stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, yet structural perception finds 1.5 to 1.8 unassigned stereocentres per molecule in the top deciles of three objectives, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture. Each session converges hard onto one substituted scaffold: the highest-scoring decile (87 molecules) holds only 12 to 21 distinct Murcko scaffolds on four of the five objectives against 187 to 560 over the full proposal set, and on one objective 83 of those 87 come from a single seed. Halogenation is the dominant edit and it lands on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon (888 of 4,350 proposals carry an N-halogen bond, 162 an O-halogen bond), while no proposal anywhere in the node contains a trihalomethyl carbon and geminal dihalides number 3 to 13 per objective. Synthetic-accessibility scores average 3.1 to 4.4 and reach 5.0 in one top decile. 98 of the 4,350 proposals carry six or fewer heavy atoms and arrive as late as evaluations 298 to 300.

per_task.generated_character: One family, decorated: a 5,6,7-polymethyl or methoxy indole-2-carboxamide with an N-aryl or N-pyridyl amide. Mean 24.3 heavy atoms, MW 369, 3.0 rings of which 2.8 are aromatic, SA 3.1 - small, flat, and the most makeable skeleton the node produces. 656 of 870 proposals carry an amide and 741 a five-membered aromatic nitrogen; the top decile is 86 of 87 amide and 83 of 87 azole, with only 12 distinct Murcko scaffolds and 27 of the 87 sharing O=C(Nc1ccncc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1. What spoils the family is halogen: digest halogen_rate is 0.9529 and 86 of the 87 top-decile molecules carry a nitrogen-halogen bond, either N-F on the indole nitrogen or N-Cl on the anilide nitrogen.
liabilities: the node best Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)cc2c(C)c1C is an N-chloroamide, an oxidant and not a storable compound
N-fluoro indoles (n2F) across the seed-1 leaders, which is not a stable arrangement of nitrogen and fluorine
the alpha-ketoamide the best molecules add is electrophilic and hydrolytically soft
10 O-halogen and 8 peroxide proposals in the same set
sub-seven-heavy-atom fragments at the end of the budget: C=COC at evaluation 299 scoring 0.0
missing_features: a halogen-free version of its own leading scaffold: halogen_rate 0.9529 over 870 proposals while the score moves not at all across F/Cl/Br swaps
an ordinary N1 substituent on the indole (N-H or N-methyl) rather than N-F or N-Cl; the one scoring initial molecule was N-H
a second bicyclic nitrogen heteroaromatic core - the top decile holds 12 scaffolds where the full set holds 187
N,N-dialkyl acetamide or nitrile side chains: 1 of 870 proposals contains a nitrile and 23 a tertiary ring nitrogen
any basic amine centre at all in the leading family: 0 of the top 87 molecules carry an sp3 basic amine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is inherited, not discovered. Of the ten initial records only COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC scored above 0.15 (0.3051); every later gain to the node best of 0.4505 stays on that indole-2-carboxamide core, trading methoxy for methyl, growing the amide to an alpha-ketoamide and moving the amide nitrogen onto pyridine. The gradient is flat in halogen identity: seven digest-best molecules tie at exactly 0.438799 while F, Cl and Br permute over two positions and the pyridyl nitrogen walks, and 165 of 870 proposals sit in five-way or larger exact score ties. The worst molecules are bare atoms and diatomics (Br, F, FCl, ClCl) at 0.0, so the objective gives nothing for fragments.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and most heteroatom-dense set: mean 31.6 heavy atoms, MW 461, 4.2 rings, 11.2 heteroatoms, TPSA 123. Two unrelated leader families. Seed 0 builds a fused purinone-triazinethione cage carrying a quinazoline whose substituents are an O-F hypofluorite and a chlorine (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3). Seed 2 builds a nitroso-anilide on a benzene fused to a three-membered ring, with a second nitroso on the aniline. Over 870 proposals: 240 nitroso, 256 nitrile, 95 thiocarbonyl, 78 peroxide, 60 anhydride-like, 55 O-halogen, and 85 molecules in which a bond is drawn across the interior of an aromatic ring - 21 of those in the top 87. Amides are nearly absent (21 of 870) and sulfonamides entirely absent (0 of 870).
liabilities: O-F hypofluorite groups in 10 of the top 87 molecules, which is a fluorinating reagent motif and not a substituent
the alpha-chloro ether C(F)OCCl on the best molecule, a hydrolytically unstable mixed halo-acetal
paired nitroso groups in 49 of the top 87, carcinogenic and tautomerically unstable where attached to N-H
transannular bonds inside benzene rings in 21 of the top 87 (the cc2-3 and cc3-4 fragments)
cyclic thiocarbonyls plus peroxides in the same proposal set (95 and 78 of 870)
SMILES up to 191 characters, far past the size the gradient actually rewards
missing_features: an amide or sulfonamide linker between core and appendage: 21 of 870 proposals are amides, 0 of 870 sulfonamides
a saturated basic appendage such as a piperidine or piperazine: 10 of 870 proposals carry a tertiary ring nitrogen
aryl ethers and biaryls with ordinary substituents instead of O-F and alpha-chloroethers
discrete azole rings joined by single bonds rather than everything fused into one cage; the top decile averages 3.1 aromatic rings inside 3.8 total rings
a second scaffold family per seed: 12 distinct Murcko scaffolds in the top 87 against 347 over the full set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective floors at 0.5: single atoms and diatomics (Cl, C=C, CBr, N=O, NCCCl) all score exactly 0.5000, and all ten initial molecules sit between 0.500 and 0.548, so half the available credit is free. Above that, score tracks the size and hetero-richness of a fused polycyclic core plus one aryl appendage; seed 0's 0.8561 is reached only by the triazinethione-purinone cage and only in the last twenty evaluations, while seeds 1 and 2 plateau near 0.62-0.64 on completely different skeletons. The top decile carries more rotatable bonds (8.5 versus 5.5 overall), so the gradient rewards appended decoration rather than a tighter core.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventionally drug-like family in the node and the one that nearly saturates: a 2-aryl-2-alkyl hexahydropyrimidine or 1,4-diazepane bearing an N-phenethyl, with a meta-chlorophenyl on the quaternary ring carbon and a bromo- or alkyl-substituted arene on the ethyl side. 718 of 870 proposals carry an sp3 basic amine and 458 a basic ring nitrogen; in the top 87 that is 87 and 83. Aryl halides appear in 835 of 870 and all 87 of the top decile. The top decile is lipophilic and bare: mean logP 5.42, TPSA 31.1, 0 amides, 0 acids, 0 sulfonamides, fraction Csp3 0.45, SA 3.72. Diversity is collapsed around one motif - 38 of the top 87 share the scaffold c1ccc(CCN2CCCNC2c2ccccc2)cc1 and 83 of the 87 come from seed 1 alone. Only 1 of 870 proposals contains a five-membered aromatic nitrogen.
liabilities: the leading motif is an aminal (N-C-N) at its key carbon, hydrolytically labile: CCCc1c(Br)cc(Br)cc1CCN1CCCNC1(CC)c1cccc(Cl)c1
halogen on the aminal carbon in several leaders, an N-C-F centre that is a masked iminium: CCc1cc(CCN2CCCNC2(F)c2cccc(Cl)c2)c(C)c(N)c1O
alpha-halo alcohols (fluorohydrin and chlorohydrin) on the leaders: CCc1c(Br)cc(C(O)F)cc1CCN1CCCNC1(CC)c1cccc(Cl)c1
top-decile mean logP 5.42 with TPSA 31, outside ordinary oral space
1.5 unassigned stereocentres per top-decile molecule, so the quoted score belongs to a mixture
a three-heavy-atom fragment proposed at evaluation 298 of 300: CCCF scoring 0.00419
missing_features: a true piperazine or piperidine instead of an aminal ring: only 17 of 870 proposals contain an N-C-C-N ring fragment and 3 of the top 87
any specified configuration at the quaternary carbon that carries the aryl group; 0 of 870 proposals specify stereochemistry
the protonated form the motif implies; digest charged_rate is 0.0 over all 870 proposals

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over this node's 4,350 optimizer proposals (five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations each, read from the staging trajectories under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-2/runs/staging), 888 molecules contain a nitrogen-halogen bond and 162 an oxygen-halogen bond, while 0 contain a trihalomethyl carbon and only 3 to 13 per objective contain even a geminal dihalide. On one objective 86 of the 87 highest-scoring molecules carry an N-halogen bond (Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)cc2c(C)c1C, CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F); on another 64 of 87 do, and that same objective's score rises with halogen count (3.45 halogens per top-decile molecule against 1.02 in the bottom decile), so the one edit it needs most is the one the operator set cannot place correctly.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogenation is applied to nitrogen and oxygen as freely as to carbon, and the generator cannot build a multiply halogenated carbon at all.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen substitution is the cheapest edit available and it is applied without regard to the element it lands on. A task-agnostic generator would treat heteroatom-halogen bond formation as its own rarely valid class rather than one more substitution, and would offer polyhalogenated carbon substituents (trihalomethyl, difluoromethylene, polyhalogenated arene) as single constructible units instead of requiring three independent single-halogen edits on one carbon that the operators never chain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest counters report charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 870 proposals on each of the five objectives. Structural perception of the same molecules finds unassigned stereocentres averaging 1.98, 1.17 and 0.98 per proposal on three objectives and 1.53 to 1.84 per molecule across their top deciles, including the quaternary aryl carbon that every leader of one objective carries (CCCc1c(Br)cc(Br)cc1CCN1CCCNC1(CC)c1cccc(Cl)c1) and the bridged cage carbons of another (CCCc1cc(N2C3CC4=C(NCN4C(=O)CN(C)C3=O)C2CC)c2ccccc2n1). 718 of 870 proposals on one objective carry a basic amine that would be protonated at physiological pH, and none is written in that state.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal carries a formal charge or a specified configuration, even where the generator's own leaders are stereogenic.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation as used cannot express configuration or protonation, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture and any surface sensitive to enantiomers, diastereomers or ionisation is being scored on an ambiguous structure. A task-agnostic generator would assign configuration when it creates a stereocentre, propose both configurations as distinct candidates, and be able to emit salt and zwitterion forms.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective 85 of 870 proposals and 21 of its top 87 contain a ring of four or fewer atoms whose every atom is aromatic, that is a bond drawn through the interior of a benzene ring (COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2); on another 59 of 870 and 12 of its top 87 do (N=c1c2c(CF)n(C3(CF)C(O)=CC=C3CF)c3c2n-3c(=O)n1CCF). On a third, 417 of 870 proposals have a smallest-ring set containing an eight-membered ring created by bridging, with 1.84 bridgehead atoms per top-decile molecule and a synthetic-accessibility score of 4.54 (CCCc1cc(N2C(C)C3=C4CC2C(=O)N(C)CC(=O)N4CC3)c2ccccc2n1).
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-editing operators create geometrically infeasible rings: bonds across aromatic rings, three- and four-membered fusions, and bridged cages with no feasibility test.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, bridging and contraction are validated by valence and canonical identity alone. A task-agnostic generator would need ring-size and planarity awareness inside those operators: refuse a new bond between two atoms of the same aromatic ring, bound bridged-cage formation to geometrically realisable bicyclic patterns, and treat a three- or four-membered fused ring as a rare class rather than a free edit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the five objectives the proposals include nitroso groups in 240 of 870 on one, 49 of them inside its top 87; oxygen-halogen hypohalites in 55 of 870 with 10 in the top 87 (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3, which also carries an alpha-chloro ether); peroxides in 78; thiocarbonyls in 95; anhydride-like groups in 60. Another objective's leaders put halogen on an aminal carbon (CCc1cc(CCN2CCCNC2(F)c2cccc(Cl)c2)) and an alpha-halo alcohol on an arene (CCc1c(Br)cc(C(O)F)cc1CCN1CCCNC1(CC)c1cccc(Cl)c1). 445 of 4,350 proposals contain an N-C-N aminal and 101 a fully substituted one.
transferable_gaps.gap: There is no stability vocabulary, so reactive and short-lived groups are attached to otherwise reasonable scaffolds and ride into the leader set.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admission tests valence, canonical novelty and one narrow inherited sulfur rule, and nothing else about chemical stability. A task-agnostic generator would classify the local environment an edit creates against a general reactivity vocabulary covering N-O, O-halogen, N-halogen, peroxide, aminal, alpha-halo ether and alpha-halo alcohol, and either refuse those environments or spend a bounded fraction of its proposals on them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 98 of this node's 4,350 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms, spread over all five objectives (20, 25, 21, 12 and 20), and they arrive as late as the final evaluations of a 300-call budget: CCCF at evaluation 298 scoring 0.00419 on one objective, C=COC at 299 scoring 0.0 on another, a bare C at 281 scoring 0.0 on a third, FF at 244 and NCCCl at 258. Bare halogens and interhalogens appear as proposals (ClCl, FF, CF, OS).
transferable_gaps.gap: Deletion operators are unbounded below, so the generator proposes single atoms and diatomics to the oracle instead of repairing them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom, bond and ring deletion have no lower bound, so a measurable slice of every fixed evaluation budget is spent on molecules too small to carry any pharmacophore. A task-agnostic generator would bound deletion by a minimum heavy-atom count or by retention of at least one ring system, and would repair or resample rather than submit the fragment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective seven proposals tie at exactly 0.438799 and differ only in whether two positions carry F, Cl or Br and where the pyridyl nitrogen sits (CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F, CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(F)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F, CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2Cl, CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)Nc1cccnc1)n2F), and 165 of its 870 proposals fall into five-way or larger exact score ties; a second objective has 79 such proposals and a third 54. The ties are concentrated in the last third of the budget.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late-budget edits permute peripheral substituent identity, producing analogue families whose scores are exactly equal.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The edit distribution concentrates on substituent identity at a few peripheral positions, the cheapest edit the operator set offers and the one least likely to move any surface. A task-agnostic generator would need skeleton edits - ring replacement, linker length, fusion pattern, scaffold hop - available at comparable frequency, and would detect that a family of proposals is returning identical values before spending more budget inside it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the highest-scoring decile of 87 molecules there are only 12, 12, 20 and 21 distinct Murcko scaffolds on four of the five objectives, against 187 to 560 distinct scaffolds over the corresponding full 870 proposals; 38 of one objective's top 87 share the single scaffold c1ccc(CCN2CCCNC2c2ccccc2)cc1 and 27 of another's share O=C(Nc1ccncc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1. On one objective 83 of the 87 best molecules come from a single seed of three, and the three seeds reach visibly different skeletons and different ceilings (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 versus COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2).
transferable_gaps.gap: Each session collapses onto one substituted scaffold and keeps no population of distinct scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator has no mechanism to hold several structurally distinct families alive at once, so each run is one scaffold's luck and the variance between seeds is scaffold variance. A task-agnostic generator would maintain an explicit multi-family population with a structural novelty or scaffold-distance term in its candidate admission, rather than editing whatever the current leader is.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five objectives start from the same ten initial records, yet sulfonamide content in the 870 proposals is 75 on one objective - 46 of them in its 87 lowest-scoring molecules, 0 in its top 87, all descendants of the one initial sulfonamide (COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1) - 1 on another and 0 on a third. Carboxylic acids run 51, 4, 1, 1 and 0; primary aliphatic amines 5 to 55; nitriles 1 on one objective against 256 on another. Amide content ranges from 656 of 870 down to 19 of 870 across objectives whose starting molecules were identical.
transferable_gaps.gap: Whole polar and ionisable functional-group classes are reachable only by inheritance from the starting molecules, never by construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Entire polar and ionisable group classes are accessible only by inheritance, so a run that drifts away from a group early can never recover it even when it is the feature being rewarded. A task-agnostic generator would need constructive introduction of sulfonyl, carboxyl, primary amine, amide and nitrile groups as first-class edits on an existing scaffold, independent of whether any surviving molecule already contains one.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
